page0.text:
We're back at my place.
I never thought we would make it back alive, so the tension in my shoulders relaxes as soon as I get in the living room.
"...Whoa."
I feel a bit dizzy and lean against the wall.

page1.text:
"See. You can't even stay standing, idiot."
"...Mrgh."

page2.text:
...Tohsaka is right, but I think that last part was unnecessary.
How many times did she call me an idiot today? I bet she set a new record today.

page3.text:
"Come here. It'll be bad if we don't at least replace those bandages."
...
I nod at her stare that won't let me say otherwise and go to Tohsaka.

page4.text:
"I can use this first-aid kit, right? Oh, as expected from a house with a dojo.
It might be because there's this many scissors in here, but it's rare to see a first-aid kit with needles and threads... Hey, hurry up. Take off your clothes and show me your wound."

page5.text: "Huh... I have to take my clothes off? Oh, no, I can do it myself. I did it this morning too, so there's no problem."

page6.text: "...Hey. I don't know why you're being so hesitant, but who do you think treated your wound in the first place?"

page7.text:
"...Oof. But that time, um..."
I was unconscious, so I was only causing an inconvenience to Tohsaka.

page8.text: "Stop whining and hurry up. Your wound is special, so we have to treat it or else it won't heal."

page9.text:
"..."
...How unfair.
I can't complain if she tells me with a face like that.

page10.text:
"...Yeah. Then I'll leave it to you. To be honest, it's been burning."
I give up and sit down.
Seeing that my clothes are stained with blood, Tohsaka gives up taking it off and starts cutting it right away. She then quickly but carefully takes off the bandages.

page11.text:
...
...It must've been bad, as Tohsaka slightly gasps.

page12.text:
"..."
...But, I'm troubled as well.
It's so embarrassing having her stare at my body so closely.

page13.text:
"You really push yourself. It was healing, but it opened up again.
...Geez. I can't get mad at you if I see a wound like this."
She talks abusively, yet gently touches my wound.

page14.text:
...
...Damn. I'm getting dizzy for a different reason.
I was calm even when we were that close earlier, but now my heart is unstable and I don't know where to look.

page15.text:
"...Oh, man."
I mutter inside and hit my boiled head, but it does no good.
The temperature inside my head will keep on going up if we stay like this.

page16.text:
"...Tohsaka? Um, that's enough, right? You can just use a styptic, antibiotic ointment, and rewrap the bandages."
"You don't call that treatment... I take it back, I am pissed. You went out with a hack job like this?"

page17.text:
A slapping sound.
"Guh...!"
W-What was that for...!?
Tohsaka slapped me on my wound without mercy...!

page18.text:
"Khh, you...! Do you have some grudge against me!?"
"Humph. You have no idea. You should thank me for going easy on you."
Saying that, she takes out something that looks like homemade ointment.

page19.text:
"That hurt, right? I healed the dead nerves, so it'll hurt for a while. There's painkiller in this ointment, but it's originally to replace your damaged flesh.
It'll hurt until it blends in, so don't do anything reckless until the pain goes away."

page20.text:
She applies the jelly-like substance on my wound.
...
It looks really suspicious, but Tohsaka is treating me seriously.

page21.text: "Here, all done. You should feel somewhat better once you wrap bandages around it and get a good night's rest."

page22.text:
She skillfully wraps the bandages around the wound.
...I'm not praising her, but her wrapping is much better than mine.

page23.text:
"...Yeah. Um, thanks, Tohsaka. I feel better."
I thank her, trying not to make eye contact.
"Huh... W-Well, that's good. I'm glad I treated you if you feel better."

page24.text:
"Yeah. It's even more helpful since I didn't think it would heal.
Anyways, thanks for treating the wound."
"...H-Heh. Of course. I'm going to heal it as long as I'm treating it."

page25.text:
Finishing the treatment, Tohsaka stands up.
...Then...
I don't know why, but she heads straight to the kitchen.

page26.text:
"Tohsaka?"
Am I seeing things?
She's checking inside the refrigerator and the rice cooker.

page27.text:
"Hey, what are you doing?"
"I'm preparing dinner. You haven't eaten yet right, Shirou? I haven't eaten either. So we're going to have dinner."

page28.text:
"...Yeah, I can tell. But, why are we having dinner in this situation?"
"It's only natural. People can't come up with decent ideas on an empty stomach, right?"

page29.text:
And...
Tohsaka declares while glaring at the inside of the refrigerator.

page30.text:
The sounds of clashing tableware echoes.
It's past 10 PM.
I don't know how it ended up like this, but I'm eating a late dinner with Tohsaka in the living room.

page31.text:
By the way, the dinner was made by both of us.
Princess Tohsaka wanted to eat Japanese cuisine, but she didn't even know how to make miso soup.
It really makes me worried what our school is teaching the girls in cooking class.

page32.text:
Tohsaka focuses on her meal.
She must be hungry, as her bowl is almost empty.

page33.text:
...
But, I don't have much of an appetite right now.
It's partly because this isn't the time to be eating, but more so because I haven't said it yet.

page34.text:
"...Withdraw now."
I haven't expressed my thoughts to Tohsaka who told me that as she left.

page35.text:
"...Tohsaka, I have something I want to talk about."
I put my chopsticks down and look at Tohsaka.

page36.text:
"What?"
"I've been thinking since then. About why I joined this battle.
And what I wanted to do."

page37.text:
"Yeah, and?"
She urges me as she sips on her miso soup.
...It puts my spirit down, but I put strength in my abdomen, refusing to lose.

page38.text:
"At first, it was because I was dragged into it. And as long as I became a Master, I wanted to do something about this war.
...But, it has nothing to do with becoming a Master or being dragged into it."

page39.text:
...
"I like being a hero of justice. That's why I need to protect everyone. I don't care about this Master thing. It makes no difference in the fact that I'm going to fight even if I'm not a Master anymore or lost Saber."

page40.text:
I said, ready for Tohsaka's rebuttal.
...But Tohsaka...
"Oh, I see."
...gives an absentminded answer and finishes the food in her bowl.

page41.text: "Hey, Tohsaka. I'm talking about serious stuff, so—"

page42.text:
"I'm listening. You're going to fight by yourself, right? You can't stand the fact that people are dying rather than the fact that you might die.
That's why you decided to fight no matter how weak you are."

page43.text:
She looks straight at me.
It's as if she sees through a part of me that even I don't know about with integrity... And approves of me fighting.

page44.text:
"Huh... Oh, yeah. That's true."
"What's with that face? You look like a squirrel that has licked sugar."
"Well, I thought you were going to object."

page45.text:
"Of course I do. But I can't complain to you when you saved me like that.
...Besides, I know that you're like that no matter how much I try to stop you."

page46.text:
Tohsaka averts her gaze a bit.
"Hm?"
I don't know why, but anyway...

page47.text:
"So Tohsaka, we're still cooperating right...!?"
"...Yeah. It can't be helped, so I'll go along with it. First of all, I'll be so worried that I won't be able to sleep soundly if I let you be on your own. And..."
She takes a deep breath.
After getting ready for some reason...

page48.text:
"To say it like you would, I don't hate you.
...That's how it is for me, so you also don't have a problem being together, right?"

page49.text:
Tohsaka hands me her bowl.
How long did it take for me to realize that she's asking for seconds?

page50.text:
"Oh... Yeah, of course...! I don't care how much of a tyrant you are; it's what I want!"
I take the bowl, open the rice cooker, swing the rice paddle, and hand it back to her with an extra portion.
"...Fine. I'm hungry and the food's good."
Tohsaka starts eating the mountain of rice.
